title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 90 (Register of significant beneficial owners)

content.overview: Section 90 requires an individual who meets the significant-beneficial-owner test—generally at least 10% of shares, voting rights or distribution rights, or significant influence/control through the holdings described in the Act and rules—to declare the interest to the company. The company must maintain a register, file prescribed returns, take steps to identify SBOs and act on non-disclosure. Failure to maintain/file/take required steps or denial of inspection attracts current company/officer penalties; wilful false declarations may engage section 447.

content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 90 (Significant beneficial ownership regime). The section addresses an individual who, alone or together with others or through one or more persons or a trust, holds the prescribed significant beneficial interest or exercises significant influence/control. The statutory threshold is generally not less than ten per cent of shares, voting rights, or the right to receive/participate in dividend or other distribution, read with the Companies (Significant Beneficial Owners) Rules and their definitions of indirect/direct holdings. The individual must declare the nature of the interest and prescribed particulars. The company must maintain a register, file prescribed returns and take steps to identify an SBO; it may issue notice where it believes a person is an SBO. If the person fails to provide required information, the company must apply to the Tribunal within the statutory period, and the Tribunal may impose restrictions on transfer or rights attached to shares. Under subsection (11), failure to maintain the register, file information, take required steps or permit inspection attracts a penalty of ₹1,00,000 for the company and, for continuing failure, ₹500 per day after the first, capped at ₹5,00,000; every officer in default is liable to ₹25,000 and, for continuing failure, ₹200 per day after the first, capped at ₹1,00,000. Wilfully furnishing false/incorrect information or suppressing material information in the declaration may engage section 447. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Significant beneficial owner threshold
sections.body: The section and applicable rules identify the individual who, alone or together with others or through one or more persons or a trust, has the prescribed significant beneficial interest or exercises significant influence/control. The statutory threshold is generally not less than ten per cent of shares, voting rights, or the right to receive or participate in dividend or other distribution, read with the rules governing indirect and direct holdings.

sections.heading: Declaration and company duties
sections.body: The individual must declare the nature of the interest and prescribed particulars to the company. The company must maintain the register of significant beneficial owners, file the prescribed return and take necessary steps to identify an SBO and require the declaration under the Act and rules.

sections.heading: Notice and Tribunal process
sections.body: Where the company has reasonable cause to believe that a person is an SBO, it may issue notice requiring information. If the person fails to provide the required information within the statutory period, the company must apply to the Tribunal within the period specified by the section. The Tribunal may restrict transfer of the interest, suspend rights attached to the shares or make other orders permitted by the section.

sections.heading: Current company/officer penalties
sections.body: Under subsection (11), failure to maintain the register, file information under subsection (4), take necessary steps under subsection (4A), or permit inspection as required attracts a penalty of ₹1,00,000 for the company and, for continuing failure, a further ₹500 per day after the first, capped at ₹5,00,000. Every officer in default is liable to ₹25,000 and, for continuing failure, a further ₹200 per day after the first, capped at ₹1,00,000.

sections.heading: False declaration
sections.body: Under subsection (12), a person who wilfully furnishes false or incorrect information or suppresses material information known to them in the declaration is liable to action under section 447.

examples.title: Layered holding
examples.body: An individual controlling a chain that holds the shares can be the significant beneficial owner even if not the registered member.

examples.title: Rights freeze
examples.body: Failure to declare can support a Tribunal order restricting transfer and voting.

hypotheticals.question: An individual indirectly holds 12% of a company's voting rights through a layered structure. What must be checked under section 90?
hypotheticals.analysis: Identify the natural person and assess the indirect/direct holding and control rules in section 90 and the Companies (Significant Beneficial Owners) Rules. If the statutory test is met, the individual must make the prescribed declaration and the company must maintain/file the required information and take the required identification steps.

hypotheticals.question: A company fails to maintain the SBO register and file required information, and the failure continues. What current penalties should be distinguished?
hypotheticals.analysis: Under subsection (11), the company is liable to ₹1,00,000 and a continuing-failure penalty of ₹500 per day after the first, capped at ₹5,00,000. Every officer in default is liable to ₹25,000 and ₹200 per day after the first, capped at ₹1,00,000.

distinctions.title: Section 89 beneficial-interest declarations and section 90 SBO regime
distinctions.left: Section 89 addresses declarations by a registered holder and beneficial owner about beneficial interest in shares.
distinctions.right: Section 90 addresses the significant beneficial owner test, including indirect holdings/control, company identification steps and the SBO register/return.

rows.left: Registered holder and beneficial owner in respect of shares
rows.right: Natural person meeting the significant beneficial ownership/control test

rows.left: Record the declaration and file the prescribed return
rows.right: Identify SBOs, maintain the register and file prescribed information

misconceptions.trap: Treating the registered shareholder as necessarily the significant beneficial owner.
misconceptions.correction: The section and rules focus on the individual behind the relevant beneficial interest or control, including through indirect holdings.

misconceptions.trap: Conflating section 89 beneficial-interest declarations with the section 90 SBO regime.
misconceptions.correction: Section 89 concerns declarations by registered holders/beneficial owners; section 90 addresses the significant beneficial owner regime and company identification duties.

misconceptions.trap: Using superseded penalty language or omitting the separate officer penalty.
misconceptions.correction: Apply the current subsection (11) penalty amounts and caps, and subsection (12) for wilful false or suppressed declaration information.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Is the registered body corporate the significant beneficial owner?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: The regime looks through to the individual. A body corporate is not itself the significant beneficial owner.
